scope: Normative interpretation of optional StructTreeRoot/K and StructElem/K null only; no product changes or conformance completion claim.
recommendation: Do not qualify direct /K null as an authoritative negative. For the hierarchy-only predicate, interpret direct or indirect null as absent when K is optional. /K [null] (and array references resolving to null) remain definite negatives.

general-rule.meaning: Null-valued dictionary entries are semantically equivalent to omission; the rule does not erase array elements.

specific-rule.Table354: K remains optional; its supplied child value or array members may not be null. The added word Values can be read as broader than array membership, creating possible tension with 7.3.7/7.3.9.
specific-rule.Table355: K remains optional; actual children may not be null. No explicit exception to dictionary null-as-absence is stated.

intent-evidence.summary: The approved issue is framed specifically around null array elements. Its author distinguishes a null inside an array from a null array value, and the July2023 summary scopes the prohibitions to array elements.

uncertainty: Public sources support preserving the general optional-entry semantics, but no explicit adjudication of the final Table354 wording versus 7.3.9 was found. Therefore the direct-null FAIL oracle is not securely established; the result should not be described as an authoritative ruling on all PDF2 structural conformance.
tests: Retain optional K absent/null equivalence as a positive hierarchy-only comparison, add root and element array-null failures, and keep required-entry-null failures because required absence is invalid. Separate rules may make omission invalid in a larger tagged-PDF context.
implementation-consequence: No new raw dictionary parser is justified merely to enforce the disputed direct-null negative. qpdf omission is compatible with general dictionary semantics.
